dvcat: a terminal UI for DVC

The problem it solves

DVC does its job, and its command line output is not friendly. Which stages are stale, and why? Did the parameters change, a dependency, the command or an output? What does the experiment table look like across five runs? The answers are there, but you have to piece them together from dvc status, dvc params diff, dvc exp show and a look into dvc.lock.

It gets worse with long pipelines. A run takes an hour on the computer at home, you close the terminal, and an hour later you do not know if it is still going, if it failed, or if someone else started a second dvc repro that is fighting for the same lock. I wanted one screen that answers all of this and stays out of the way.

The general idea

The goal: use DVC in a friendly way without VS Code. The editor extensions give you a pipeline view, an experiments table and plots, but they tie you to a graphical editor, and I work in the terminal, often over SSH. dvcat (DVC and cat) brings the same things to any terminal.

dvcat is written in Rust with ratatui: one fast binary with no runtime to install. It is a minimal terminal UI for DVC, in Catppuccin Mocha colours (it needs a true-colour terminal). It does not replace DVC and it does not store anything about your pipeline. It reads dvc.yaml, dvc.lock and params.yaml, calls the real dvc for everything that changes something, and shows you the result. The views:

  • Pipeline. A list of stages with a status glyph, a detail pane and a files pane. ✓ is up to date, ● stale, ○ never run, ? unverified and … still checking.
  • Graph. The stages as boxes in dependency layers, left to right, with an arrow for each dependency. The cursor is shared with the pipeline view.
  • Experiments. A table of all experiments with their params and metrics, sortable, with differences from the baseline, a chart and actions.
  • Plots. The plots: section of dvc.yaml drawn in the terminal from your CSV, TSV, JSON or YAML files, with a form to add new plots.

Examples

cargo install --git https://github.com/MarcellGranat/dvcat --locked

cd my-dvc-project
dvcat                    # or: dvcat path/to/project

Why is this stage stale?

A stage is stale when its command, parameters, dependencies or recorded outputs differ from dvc.lock. The detail pane tells you which of the four, and which one exactly: the parameter that changed, a deleted output (missing output: data/clean.parquet) or an edited one (modified output: ...). Outputs are compared by size first and hashed only when the size matches, so the check is fast. Directories and files over 256 MiB are shown as unverified instead of slowing you down.

Run, watch, cancel

r runs the selected stage only (dvc repro --single-item), R runs it together with its stale upstream stages (dvc repro), and x cancels. The log is live, the title shows how long the run has taken, and the stage list remembers the duration of the last run. DVC keeps no durations itself, so this is stored in .dvc/tmp/dvcat-history.json, inside DVC's own Git-ignored tmp directory.

Experiments

The table shows every experiment with its params and metrics. A param that differs from the baseline is highlighted, and m turns the metric cells into signed differences such as ▲ +0.1867. The arrows show direction only, because the tool cannot know if higher or lower is better. From the table you can:

  • n start a new experiment. A form lists every param, pre-filled from the row under the cursor, and only the values you changed become -S overrides. The command that will run is shown at the bottom, and it runs as dvc exp run --temp in an isolated copy, so your workspace stays untouched.
  • a apply, d remove, b save the experiment as a Git branch. Each asks a yes/no question first, and the branch is created without checking it out.
  • c write or edit the message of an experiment, the text of dvc exp run -m. It is shown under the table, so a row named lr-005 can also say "smaller learning rate, after fixing the join".
  • s sort, t transpose the table, v choose which params are shown (grouped by file, so train.* can be hidden at once) and p chart one metric against a param.

Messages: notes on every experiment

Experiment names such as exp-3f9a1 tell you nothing a week later. DVC can store a message with every experiment (dvc exp run -m "..."), and almost nobody looks at it because dvc exp show hides it. dvcat shows the message of the experiment under the cursor below the table, and c edits it. It becomes a habit to write one line about why you tried the run, and the table turns into a lab notebook.

Plots

Press 4 or p for the plots view. It draws everything in the plots: section of dvc.yaml as a chart in the terminal, reading the data from the workspace. dvcat saves nothing of its own: the definitions stay in dvc.yaml and the data in your tracked files, exactly as in DVC.

  • j/k pick a plot, F5 re-reads the files after a run, and d shows the plot's definition from dvc.yaml under the chart.
  • n opens a form for a new plot: the data file, x, y, the template and a title. The form lists the columns of the file, and Ctrl+F picks the file with fzf. The plot is added to the plots: section and the rest of the file is left untouched.
  • Supported: x, y (a field, a list, or file: fields), titles, axis labels and the templates linear, simple, scatter, smooth, bar_horizontal, bar_horizontal_sorted, confusion and confusion_normalized.
plots:
  - metrics/loss.csv:
      x: epoch
      y: loss
      title: Training loss

Adding a stage

In the pipeline and graph views n opens a form for a new stage: name, command, dependencies, params, outputs and metrics, with toggles for cache, persist, always_changed and frozen. Ctrl+F on a list field picks files, or param keys, with fzf. The stage is written to dvc.yaml and nothing else in the file changes.

Templated stages

foreach, matrix and vars in dvc.yaml are expanded the way DVC does it, so a stage like each@us or grid@lin-1 is listed, checked and runnable like any other. A stage that uses something dvcat does not understand is shown with a warning and the reason instead of being silently wrong.

Keys

  • j/k move, Tab switches between the stages and the files pane, Enter steps into a stage's files or previews a file, o opens it in $EDITOR.
  • 1 2 3 4 switch between the pipeline, graph, experiments and plots.
  • q quits, and a running stage keeps running.

Tips from my setup

  • Staleness with a reason. That is the view I missed most. I no longer run dvc repro to find out what would run: I look at the list, read why, and decide.
  • A run survives the UI. Runs started from dvcat are detached. Quitting with q leaves the stage running, and the next dvcat in the project shows the output so far and keeps streaming, with the time counted from the real start. A run that finished while the interface was closed is shown once, with its log, outcome and duration. This fits long runs on the computer at home that I check from my phone. See the post about working from anywhere.
  • It notices runs it did not start. Every couple of seconds dvcat reads .dvc/tmp/rwlock. If another terminal or another tool is running dvc, the header names the command and its age, and the stages it works on get a marker. Pressing r on a stage that would clash with it is refused with the reason, for example which folder the other run is writing. X stops the outside process after a yes, with SIGTERM first and SIGKILL after five seconds.
  • It finds DVC through the project. dvcat looks for $DVCAT_DVC, then .venv/bin/dvc in the project, then the path, so it works with the uv setup and no global install.
  • It checks itself against DVC. One of the tests compares dvcat's stale detection with the real dvc status --json, so a difference between the two is a bug that fails the build.
  • Try it without your own pipeline. just demo builds a small Git project with three finished experiments (lr-001, lr-005, lr-010) and opens it, so you can try the table, the chart and the graph straight away.
  • What it does not do yet. It cannot show image plots, and it does not compare revisions (dvc plots diff).
  • It edits dvc.yaml carefully. The stage and plot forms only add their own block, so nothing else in the file changes and the Git diff stays small.
